name: Delft
significance: Where Leeuwenhoek ground his own lenses and made the first documented observations of microorganisms in pond water.

name: Paris
significance: Site of Pasteur's swan-neck flask experiments disproving spontaneous generation, and later the Pasteur Institute's 1983 isolation of HIV.

name: Berlin
significance: Where Koch formulated his postulates and identified the tuberculosis bacillus, founding modern medical bacteriology.

name: Vienna
significance: Site of the maternity clinic where Semmelweis showed hand-washing with chlorinated lime sharply reduced childbed fever.

name: London
significance: St Mary's Hospital, where Fleming discovered penicillin, and the same year Griffith demonstrated bacterial transformation nearby.

name: Hong Kong
significance: Where Yersin isolated the plague bacillus during the Third Plague Pandemic.

name: Zululand
significance: Where Bruce identified the trypanosome causing nagana in cattle, later linked to African sleeping sickness.

name: Rio de Janeiro
significance: Where Chagas uniquely described the parasite, insect vector, and clinical disease now known as Chagas disease.

name: Tunis
significance: Where Nicolle and Manceaux first observed Toxoplasma gondii in a local rodent, the gundi, giving the parasite its name.

name: Kolkata
significance: Where the parasite causing visceral leishmaniasis (kala-azar) was identified.

name: Valletta
significance: Where Bruce identified the bacterium causing Malta fever among British garrison troops.

name: Bergen
significance: Where Hansen identified the leprosy bacillus, the first bacterium ever linked to a human disease.

name: Tokyo
significance: Site of Kitasato's first pure culture of the tetanus bacillus and, in 1898, Shiga's identification of the dysentery bacillus.

name: Perth
significance: Where Marshall and Warren identified Helicobacter pylori as the cause of stomach ulcers, with Marshall famously self-testing the organism.

name: Yellowstone National Park
significance: Where Brock discovered Thermus aquaticus in a hot spring; its heat-stable enzyme later enabled PCR.

name: Cold Spring Harbor, New York
significance: Site of the Hershey-Chase experiment, which confirmed DNA as the genetic material using bacteriophages.

name: New Haven, Connecticut
significance: Where Lederberg and Tatum discovered bacterial conjugation, founding bacterial genetics.

name: Cambridge
significance: Where Watson and Crick built the double-helix model of DNA using X-ray data from Rosalind Franklin's lab at King's College London.

name: Wuhan
significance: Where SARS-CoV-2 was first identified and sequenced following a cluster of pneumonia cases.

name: Yambuku
significance: Village near the Ebola River where the Ebola virus was first identified during a fatal outbreak.

name: Sofia
significance: Where Grigorov isolated Lactobacillus delbrueckii subsp. bulgaricus from traditional Bulgarian yogurt.

name: Vulcano
significance: Volcanic island where Stetter isolated the hyperthermophilic archaeon Pyrococcus furiosus from marine sediment.

name: Iceland
significance: Site of the hydrothermal vent where Nanoarchaeum equitans, founder of a new archaeal phylum, was discovered.

name: Galapagos Rift
significance: Where deep-sea hydrothermal vent ecosystems sustained by chemosynthetic bacteria were first discovered.

name: Berkeley, California
significance: Where Doudna's lab helped develop CRISPR-Cas9 into a programmable gene-editing tool.

name: Rockville, Maryland
significance: Where the first complete bacterial genome, Haemophilus influenzae, was sequenced.

name: Panama City
significance: Where Darling first described Histoplasma capsulatum, initially mistaken for a protozoan parasite.

name: Buenos Aires
significance: Where Posadas first described Coccidioides immitis from a soldier's skin lesions.

name: Alicante
significance: Where Mojica identified the repeated DNA sequences in archaea and bacteria later understood as the CRISPR immune system.

name: Edinburgh
significance: Where Ogston identified Staphylococcus aureus in surgical abscess pus, linking bacteria directly to suppuration.

name: Berkeley, Gloucestershire
significance: Where Jenner developed and tested the first vaccine, using cowpox material to confer immunity against smallpox.

name: New Brunswick, New Jersey
significance: Rutgers University laboratory where streptomycin was isolated from Streptomyces griseus.

name: Baltimore, Maryland
significance: Johns Hopkins University, where restriction enzyme research enabled recombinant DNA technology.

name: San Francisco Bay Area, California
significance: Stanford and UCSF, where the first recombinant DNA organism was created, and later where Genentech engineered E. coli to produce human insulin.

name: Urbana-Champaign, Illinois
significance: University of Illinois laboratory where 16S rRNA sequencing revealed Archaea as a distinct domain of life.

name: Madison, Wisconsin
significance: Where transduction, the phage-mediated transfer of bacterial genes, was discovered.

name: New York City, New York
associatedWith: Oswald Avery; Colin MacLeod; Maclyn McCarty
significance: Rockefeller Institute, where DNA was identified as the molecule carrying genetic information.

name: Umea
significance: Where Charpentier's research on bacterial immune systems contributed to the development of CRISPR-Cas9 gene editing.

name: East Pacific hydrothermal vents
significance: Deep-sea vent site where Methanocaldococcus jannaschii was discovered, later the first archaeon fully genome-sequenced.

name: Algiers
significance: Where Laveran first observed the malaria parasite in a patient's blood while serving as a military doctor.
